wifi.title: Wi-Fi adapter
wifi.join: Join the adapter’s Wi-Fi network first (usually WiFi_OBDII, no password). On Android, if the phone warns the network has no internet, choose Stay connected.
wifi.address: Adapter address: {{endpoint}} — change it in Settings → Developer & simulator → Adapter source.

ble.noDevicesAndroid: No devices yet. Plug in the adapter, switch the ignition on, then scan. If the adapter is already paired in Android’s Bluetooth settings it may have stopped advertising — “Forget” it there first, or connect by address below.
ble.noDevices: No devices yet. Plug in the adapter, switch the ignition on, then scan.
ble.iosHint: If the adapter is not listed, turn it off and on; iOS does not pair OBD2 BLE adapters in Settings.
ble.byAddressHelp: If the adapter never shows up in the scan, copy its Bluetooth MAC (from Android Settings → Bluetooth) and connect directly.
ble.useSpp: Using a classic Bluetooth (3.0) adapter instead?

prompt.offIos: Open Control Center and turn Bluetooth on to scan for your OBD2 adapter.

spp.title: Paired adapters
spp.help: Classic Bluetooth (“3.0”) adapters connect as a paired device — pick yours below. The bus sniffer is not available over classic Bluetooth.
spp.pairFirst: Pair the adapter first: Android Settings → Bluetooth → pair OBDII (PIN 1234 or 0000), then come back.
spp.permissionDenied: Bluetooth permission denied. Allow “Nearby devices” for Bolid Tester in system settings, then refresh the list.

web.note: Works in Chrome and Edge on a computer or an Android phone, over HTTPS. Not in Safari, Firefox or on an iPhone.
web.unsupportedTitle: Bluetooth adapters are not supported in this browser
web.unsupported: This browser cannot talk to Bluetooth adapters. Use Chrome or Edge on a computer or on Android, over HTTPS — Safari, Firefox and every iPhone browser do not support Web Bluetooth. The simulator still works here.
web.instructions: Plug the adapter into the OBD2 port and switch the ignition on. The browser then lists nearby Bluetooth devices — pick your OBD2 adapter (often named OBDII, Vgate or IOS-Vlink).

wifiUnreachable.title: Can’t reach the Wi-Fi adapter
wifiUnreachable.explanation: The phone is not on the adapter’s Wi-Fi network, or the adapter uses a different address.
wifiUnreachable.s1: Join the adapter’s Wi-Fi network (usually “WiFi_OBDII”, no password). On Android, choose “Stay connected” if the phone warns the network has no internet.
wifiUnreachable.s2: Check the adapter’s address: most use 192.168.0.10, port 35000 (Settings → Developer & simulator → Adapter source).
wifiUnreachable.s3: Turn mobile data off, so the phone does not send the connection over the mobile network instead.
wifiUnreachable.s4: On iPhone, allow Local Network for Bolid Tester (Settings → Privacy & Security → Local Network).

sppUnreachable.title: Can’t open the Classic Bluetooth adapter
sppUnreachable.explanation: The adapter is paired but not reachable.
sppUnreachable.s1: Power-cycle the adapter: unplug it for 10 seconds, plug it back in, then reconnect.
sppUnreachable.s2: Make sure no other app (e.g. Torque) holds the connection — close it, or turn its auto-connect off.
sppUnreachable.s3: Keep the phone close to the adapter, with the ignition on.
sppUnreachable.s4: Still failing? Unpair the adapter in Android Settings → Bluetooth, pair it again (PIN 1234 or 0000), then refresh the list.

btPermission.title: Bluetooth permission needed
btPermission.explanation: Bolid Tester is not allowed to use Bluetooth, so it cannot reach the adapter.
btPermission.s1: Open system settings and allow “Nearby devices” (Android) or Bluetooth (iOS) for Bolid Tester.
btPermission.s2: Come back here and connect again.

bleUnsupported.title: Bluetooth LE not available
bleUnsupported.explanation: This device doesn’t support Bluetooth Low Energy, so a wireless OBD2 adapter can’t be used.
bleUnsupported.s1: Use a phone or tablet with Bluetooth Low Energy.
bleUnsupported.s2: Explore the app with the built-in simulator (Settings → Developer & simulator → Adapter source).

btOff.title: Bluetooth is off
btOff.explanation: The phone’s Bluetooth radio is off, so the app can’t reach the adapter.
btOff.s1: Turn Bluetooth on (Quick Settings on Android, Control Center on iOS).
btOff.s2: Scan for the adapter again once it is on.

notBleSerial.title: Not a Bluetooth LE serial adapter
notBleSerial.explanation: This device does not expose the serial-over-BLE characteristics an ELM327 uses — it may be a classic Bluetooth (SPP) adapter, which connects as a paired device instead.
notBleSerial.s1: Check that you picked the OBD2 adapter, not another nearby device.
notBleSerial.s2: A classic Bluetooth (“3.0”) adapter: on Android, pair it in the phone’s Bluetooth settings and choose Classic Bluetooth (Settings → Developer & simulator → Adapter source). iPhones cannot use classic adapters.
notBleSerial.s3: Scan again and pick the adapter by name (Vlink, OBDII, VEEPEAK…).

adapterSilent.title: Adapter not answering
adapterSilent.explanation: The adapter accepted the link but did not answer `ATZ` — it is unpowered or asleep.
adapterSilent.s1: Check the adapter is pushed fully into the OBD2 port and its light is on.
adapterSilent.s2: Wake it: unplug the adapter for 10 seconds, plug it back in, then reconnect.
adapterSilent.s3: Move the phone closer to the adapter.
adapterSilent.s4wifi: Still failing? Check the phone is still on the adapter’s Wi-Fi network.
adapterSilent.s4spp: Still failing? Close any other OBD2 app that may hold the adapter, then reconnect.
adapterSilent.s4ble: Still failing? Remove the adapter from the phone’s Bluetooth list and scan again.

carSilent.title: The car is not answering
carSilent.explanation: The adapter is working, but the car’s engine computer did not answer the first OBD2 request (“0100”). This almost always means the ignition is off.
carSilent.s1: Turn the ignition to ON — engine running is most reliable.
carSilent.s2: Check the adapter is fully seated in the OBD2 port.

busInit.title: Could not start the diagnostic bus
busInit.explanation: The adapter could not open a session on the car’s bus (“UNABLE TO CONNECT” / “BUS INIT”). Older cars use the slow K-line bus, which needs the ignition on and a few seconds to start.
busInit.s1: Turn the ignition to ON and wait 5 seconds before connecting.
busInit.s2: Reconnect — a K-line start-up often succeeds on the second try.
busInit.s3: Check the adapter is fully seated in the OBD2 port.
busInit.s4: Check the car has OBD2 / EOBD (EU: petrol from 2001, diesel from 2004).

linkStalled.title: The link stopped answering
linkStalled.explanation: The car answered at first, but a request timed out while the app was reading the car’s details — the {{link}} or the adapter stalled.
linkStalled.s2: Move the phone closer to the adapter.
linkStalled.s3: If it keeps happening, unplug the adapter for 10 seconds and plug it back in.

failed.title: Connection failed
failed.unknown: The connection failed for an unknown reason.
failed.unknownTo: The connection to {{device}} failed for an unknown reason.
failed.s1: Check the adapter is plugged in and its light is on.
failed.s2: Move the phone closer to the adapter.
failed.s3wifi: Rejoin the adapter’s Wi-Fi network, then reconnect.
failed.s3bt: Turn Bluetooth off and on again, then reconnect.
failed.s4: Open the error log for the technical details.

service.linkLost: Adapter link lost — the connection dropped unexpectedly. Check the adapter is seated in the OBD2 port and reconnect.
service.flapPaused: The link dropped 3 times in a minute — auto-reconnect paused. Check the adapter is seated and reconnect manually.
service.reconnecting: Reconnecting to the adapter… attempt {{attempt}} of {{total}}.
service.reconnectFailed_one: Auto-reconnect failed after {{count}} attempt. Reconnect manually when the adapter is powered and back in range.
service.reconnectFailed_other: Auto-reconnect failed after {{count}} attempts. Reconnect manually when the adapter is powered and back in range.

scan.permissionDenied: Bluetooth permission denied. Allow “Nearby devices” (Android 12+) or Location (Android 11 and below) for Bolid Tester in system settings, turn Bluetooth on, then scan again.
scan.permissionDeniedIos: Bluetooth permission denied. Allow Bluetooth for Bolid Tester in Settings → Bolid Tester, then scan again.
scan.off: Bluetooth is off. Turn Bluetooth on, then scan again.
scan.settling: Bluetooth is not ready yet. Wait a moment, then scan again.
